summary: Connect maintenance work, critical spares, and KPIs with practical exercises. Explore the five-day course and review the syllabus.
lede: Maintenance planning and spare-parts optimisation helps teams link work-order evidence to asset and stock priorities. For maintenance managers, reliability engineers, asset managers, planners and procurement professionals, the practical work includes ranking asset criticality with FMEA, analysing CMMS and stock data in Excel, and setting replenishment rules around demand and lead times. Participants also interpret maintenance KPIs and outline predictive-maintenance business cases to support job readiness, inventory decisions and asset uptime.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who coordinate maintenance work, asset availability, and spare-parts decisions in asset-intensive operations. This course is designed for: Maintenance managers prioritising backlogs, shutdown work, and maintenance resources. Reliability engineers analysing failure patterns and recommending maintenance tasks. Asset managers aligning criticality rankings with asset-management plans. Maintenance planners preparing job plans, schedules, labour, and material requirements. Maintenance supervisors coordinating work orders and execution readiness. Warehouse managers setting service levels and replenishment rules for maintenance spares. Inventory analysts segmenting spare parts by value, movement, and demand variability. Procurement professionals managing lead times and sourcing risks for critical spares. Operations leaders balancing equipment availability with production and maintenance windows. Energy, mining, transport, and utility engineers assessing equipment maintenance needs.
prerequisites: Working familiarity with maintenance, asset operations, planning, warehouse, or procurement processes is recommended. No coding or programming is required. Bring a laptop with Excel access; sanitized work-order or inventory examples may support exercises if your organization permits their use.
